grammar.title: 把-sentences: saying where something ends up
grammar.pattern: Subject + 把 + (definite) Object + Verb + 在/到 + Place
grammar.explanation: Use 把 to move the object in front of the verb when you want to say what you do to it and where it ends up. The object must be something both speakers already know about (你的鉛筆, 這些詞語, 課本), and the verb needs a result after it — usually 在/到 + a place, or 下來/起來. This is very common in the classroom: 把…寫在黑板上, 把…放在桌子上.
grammar.contrast: Plain SVO (我寫句子) just reports the action; 把 (我把句子寫在黑板上) focuses on what happens to a specific, already-known object. If the object is new or indefinite (我要寫一個句子), you cannot use 把.
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English word order and say 我寫句子在黑板上, or they leave the 把-sentence unfinished, like 我把鉛筆放 — a 把 sentence always needs a result after the verb (放在桌子上, 寫下來).

dialogue.gloss: Okay, I'll review as soon as I get home. Thank you, teacher!

passage.title: 我的三年級
passage.hanzi: 我是三年級的學生。我最喜歡上國語課。老師常常把新的詞語和句子寫在黑板上，我就用鉛筆把它們記在本子上。回家以後，我會先複習今天的課，再寫作業。媽媽說，每天複習一點，考試就不難了。
passage.gloss: I'm a third-grade student. My favourite class is Chinese. The teacher often writes new words and sentences on the blackboard, and I use my pencil to note them down in my notebook. After I get home, I review today's lesson first and then do my homework. Mum says if you review a little every day, tests won't be hard.

grammar.title: Describing how an action is done: V + 得 + (很) + Adjective
grammar.pattern: 主語 + (賓語) + 動詞 + 得 + 很/太 + 形容詞
grammar.explanation: To say how well or how fast someone does something, put 得 right after the verb and then an adjective. The adjective almost always needs a degree word like 很 or 太 in front of it. If there is an object, either move it to the front (他普通話說得很好) or repeat the verb (他說普通話說得很好).
grammar.contrast: Easily confused with the modifier 的: 他說的話 ("the words he said" — 的 + noun) versus 他說得很好 ("he speaks well" — 得 + adjective). If an adjective describing the action follows, use 得; if a noun follows, use 的. Both are pronounced "de".
grammar.common_error: Learners drop the 很 and say 他普通話說得好, which sounds unfinished or like a comparison, and they also put the adjective before the verb (他很好說普通話) instead of after 得.

examples.pinyin: Tā pǔtōnghuà shuō de hěn qīngchu.

examples.hanzi: 我爬山爬得很慢，可是我不著急。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ pá shān pá de hěn màn, kěshì wǒ bù zhāojí.
examples.gloss: I climb mountains very slowly, but I'm not in a hurry.

examples.pinyin: Tā yòng zìdiǎn chá de hěn kuài.
examples.gloss: She looks things up in the dictionary very fast.

grammar.title: 別 + Verb：telling someone not to do something
grammar.explanation: 別 before a verb makes a soft negative command, very common in spoken Taiwan Mandarin: 別著急 "don't worry", 別哭 "don't cry". Adding 了 at the end asks the person to stop what they are already doing.
grammar.contrast: 不要 means the same but sounds stronger and more direct; 不 + verb is just a statement (我不著急 "I'm not worried"), not a command.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 不著急 when they mean "don't panic" — that only states a fact about themselves; a command needs 別 or 不要.

examples.pinyin: Bié zhāojí, wǒmen hái yǒu shíjiān.
examples.gloss: Don't worry, we still have time.

examples.pinyin: Bié wàng le dài zhàoxiàngjī o.
examples.gloss: Don't forget to bring the camera.

examples.hanzi: 下雨了，今天別去爬山了。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, jīntiān bié qù pá shān le.
examples.gloss: It's raining; let's not go hiking today.

dialogue.speaker: 美美
dialogue.hanzi: 阿明，這個週末你有空嗎？我們去爬山。
dialogue.pinyin: Ā-Míng, zhège zhōumò nǐ yǒu kòng ma? Wǒmen qù pá shān.
dialogue.gloss: A-Ming, are you free this weekend? Let's go hiking.

dialogue.speaker: 阿明
dialogue.hanzi: 好啊！爬山也是我的愛好耶。要帶照相機嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a! Pá shān yě shì wǒ de àihào ye. Yào dài zhàoxiàngjī ma?
dialogue.gloss: Sure! Hiking is my hobby too. Should we bring a camera?

dialogue.speaker: 美美
dialogue.hanzi: 要，山上的花很漂亮。我朋友是外國人，他也想去，他的普通話說得很好。
dialogue.pinyin: Yào, shān shàng de huā hěn piàoliang. Wǒ péngyǒu shì wàiguó rén, tā yě xiǎng qù, tā de pǔtōnghuà shuō de hěn hǎo.
dialogue.gloss: Yes, the flowers on the mountain are beautiful. My friend is a foreigner and wants to come too; he speaks Mandarin very well.

dialogue.speaker: 阿明
dialogue.hanzi: 太好了！他不懂的字，我們可以幫他查字典。
dialogue.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Tā bù dǒng de zì, wǒmen kěyǐ bāng tā chá zìdiǎn.
dialogue.gloss: Great! For characters he doesn't know, we can help him look them up in a dictionary.

dialogue.speaker: 美美
dialogue.hanzi: 我們搭捷運去，八點在捷運站見。別著急，我會帶水。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒmen dā jiéyùn qù, bā diǎn zài jiéyùn zhàn jiàn. Bié zhāojí, wǒ huì dài shuǐ.
dialogue.gloss: We'll take the MRT; see you at the MRT station at eight. Don't worry, I'll bring water.

sentences.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ yào qù pá shān.
Wǒmen hái yǒu shíjiān, nǐ bùyòng zhāojí.
sentences.gloss: We still have time; you don't need to worry.

sentences.pinyin: Pá shān shì tā de àihào.
Zhège zì wǒ yào chá zìdiǎn.
sentences.gloss: I need to look this character up in the dictionary.

sentences.pinyin: Tā de pǔtōnghuà shuō de hěn qīngchu.

passage.title: 我的愛好
passage.hanzi: 我的愛好是爬山。每個週末，我都會搭捷運到山下，慢慢爬上去。我的照相機很輕，我喜歡照山上的花和小鳥。上個月，我在山上遇到一個外國人，他的普通話說得很清楚。他問我路，我不懂他說的一個字，就拿出手機查字典。他笑著說：「別著急，我們慢慢講。」
passage.gloss: My hobby is hiking. Every weekend I take the MRT to the foot of the mountain and climb up slowly. My camera is very light, and I like to photograph the flowers and little birds on the mountain. Last month I ran into a foreigner up there; he spoke Mandarin very clearly. He asked me for directions, and when I didn't understand one word he said, I took out my phone to look it up in the dictionary. He smiled and said, "Don't worry, let's talk slowly."
